title: Contract addendum: guaranteed serve-capacity and autoscale safeguards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Large customers purchasing Dedicated capacity require contractual clarity tying throughput guarantees to autoscaling behavior and fleet controls. Current contract templates enumerate per-minute or per-hour throughput entitlements but do not explicitly cover rolling autoscale events, multi-region fallback, or short-lived degradation windows caused by balancing and kernel scheduling. This ticket proposes a concise contractual addendum and measurement model that: (1) defines a measurable throughput SLO for Dedicated customers that accounts for autoscale cooldown and warm-up, (2) specifies an error-budget calculus for credits and remediation tied to sustained degradation rather than transient fluctuations, and (3) prescribes fleet control obligations and rollback triggers for the platform team.
scope: Deliver: (A) Proposed legal addendum language that can be attached to Dedicated contracts; (B) Measurement spec for telemetry and dashboards; (C) Error budget and credit computation examples; (D) Suggested autoscale policy constraints to guarantee the SLO; (E) Runbook checklist for incident vs. contractual breach determinations.
acceptance_criteria: Draft addendum reviewed by Legal and Revenue Ops
Telemetry spec implemented in Console dashboards showing per-customer throughput and warm-up windows
Example error-budget calculations for 5 customers with different entitlements included
Autoscale policy proposal (min/max capacity, warm-up, headroom) agreed with Infra leads
Operational runbook created and linked to contract language with deterministic breach-to-credit mapping
decisions: Use a 30-minute rolling measurement window for determining sustained degradation (decision made 2026-03-04, agreed with infra)
Credits will be calculated on effective served tokens relative to committed throughput averaged over a 24-hour warranty window (decision pending Legal sign-off)
Transient degradation (<3 minutes) will not count toward contractual breaches unless part of a repeated pattern identified by threshold crossings
proposed_sla_summary: Committed throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec) guaranteed per contract. Measurement uses 30-minute rolling windows with a 24-hour aggregation period for credit calculation. Platform may autoscale but must honor a configured min-reserve and controlled warm-up (see autoscale constraints). When committed throughput falls below 95% for more than two 30-minute windows in a 24-hour period, the customer is eligible for credit per the formulas in the addendum.
error_budget_and_credit_examples: Example A: Customer with 100k tokens/min entitlement. Observed effective served tokens aggregated to 88k tokens/min averaged over 24 hours with two 30-minute windows at 70k. Credit = (committed - served) / committed * monthly fee * 0.5 for first remediation tier => computation shown in Confluence link

Example B: For bursty workloads with autoscale warm-up configured to 5 minutes, the warm-up allowance excludes the first 5 minutes after a scale event from breach calculations. Repeated warm-ups (>=3 within 1 hour) remove warm-up exemptions and count toward error budget.
autoscale_policy_constraints: To make guarantees actionable we recommend the Dedicated autoscale policy include: (1) minimum reserve capacity (customer-configurable) that cannot be preempted during scale-up; (2) predictable warm-up period configurable per customer but defaulting to 5 minutes; (3) headroom buffer of 10-20% of committed throughput to accommodate sudden request spikes; (4) limits on frequency of scale events (cooldown 10 minutes) to avoid oscillation; (5) automatic fallback to a compatible model variant with documented QoS if autoscale cannot provision capacity within SLA window.
fleet_controls_and_rollback_triggers: Fleet controls required to support the SLA: tag-backed customer pools, priority routing to honor reserved pools, near-real-time quota enforcement, and regional failover agreements. Rollback triggers include: kernel/runtime regression that increases p95 latency by >25% for more than 1 hour, missed scheduled capacity commitments for >2 consecutive 30-minute windows, or systemic autoscaler failure. Rollback decisions must follow the runbook and are subject to legal notification windows defined in the addendum.
contract_language_outline: We propose a short addendum section with these parts: (1) Definitions: committed throughput, measurement window, warm-up exemption, autoscale event, breach, credit tiers; (2) Measurement & Reporting: telemetry endpoints, customer visibility, reporting cadence; (3) Remedies: credit formula, notice & cure periods, maximum monthly credit cap; (4) Operational Obligations: autoscale behavior, maintenance windows, notified capacity reductions; (5) Exceptions: planned maintenance, customer error, force majeure. Language draft linked in Confluence.
runbook_and_operational_playbook: Create a playbook that maps telemetry signals to contractual outcomes: how to distinguish transient vs. sustained degradation, logging requirements for warm-up events, manual remediation steps (drain/restore), communication templates for customer notifications, and a legal escalation path. The runbook will include a checklist used by SRE on-call to document breach windows and remediation steps to support credit calculation.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Tight guarantees with small warm-up allowances reduce customer-experienced degradation but increase cost (reserved capacity headroom) and complexity of autoscaler rules. A lenient policy reduces cost but increases exposure to customer dissatisfaction and escalation. We must balance headroom vs. price; recommend offering tiered guarantees (Standard, Premium) to let customers choose economics vs. strictness.
